operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers everywhere (Film_ID, Gross_in_dollar, film_market_estimation); must double-quote in generated SQL.
Tiny tables (13/6/9 rows) — no huge-table sampling path exercised; original_values fully read.
All declared types are INT/REAL/TEXT; no Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year dispatch, no crash-fallback types.
Column named 'Year' is declared INT and stores integers (1945,1487) — dispatches to Number, not the year fuzzer (type is 'int', not 'year').
Column named 'Type' is TEXT — dispatches to String, not a special type.
REAL columns (Low_Estimate, High_Estimate) store real storage class; Number fuzzer with scale=0 (no args) will produce ints/floats in [-1,1] — far from 80000-scale values.
FKs film_market_estimation.Film_ID->film.Film_ID and .Market_ID->market.Market_ID both resolve; parents exist and are unique PKs.
film_market_estimation.Film_ID distinct=4, Market_ID distinct=3 — many-to-one child rows; FK draw with replacement will create duplicates.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE beyond PKs; all columns nullable in DDL.
No self-references, no composite keys, no dangling FKs, no text-stored dates.
Table order: film, market at level 0; film_market_estimation at level 1 (depends on both).
Gross_in_dollar values ~1e8-4e8; Number fuzzer range [-1,1] (scale 0) makes fresh draws implausible.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Film_ID/Market_ID/Estimation_ID: fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs will be tiny ints, often negative or 0.
Number fuzzer on Gross_in_dollar: same [-1,1] range — gross values become ~0, destroying any 'gross > X' predicate selectivity.
Number fuzzer on Low_Estimate/High_Estimate (REAL, scale 0): values in [-1,1]; original 80000-scale lost; Low<=High ties unlikely to be preserved.
Number fuzzer on Year: values in [-1,1] plus perturbation; years become 0/1/-1 — 'Year BETWEEN 1940 AND 1950' returns nothing.
String fuzzer on Title/Studio/Director/Country/Type: 5 original samples + pool literals, then 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop char); names become garbled but plausible-ish.
String fuzzer on Type: only 3 distinct originals; fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() will not match 'Mass suicide' family — equality predicates on Type mostly miss.
FK fill: film_market_estimation.Film_ID drawn from film.Film_ID final values (tiny ints), Market_ID from market.Market_ID — joins still work but child rows collapse to few distinct parents.
PK dedup: Film_ID/Market_ID/Estimation_ID fresh draws in [-1,1] give ~3-5 distinct values, so 13/6/9-row tables collapse to a handful of rows after sample_fresh_primary_keys.
Likely FN driver: implausible numeric ranges (gross, year, estimates) make range/equality predicates return empty on generated instances.

Likely FP driver: missing ties/duplicates — original has repeated Film_ID/Market_ID in estimation (4/3 distinct over 9 rows); TS PK dedup on parents plus FK-with-replacement may or may not reproduce the same multiplicity, so COUNT/GROUP BY queries can differ.
String contaminate (drop first/last char) can turn 'USA' into 'US'/'SA' — LIKE/equality on Country may spuriously match or miss.
